rules.instruction: When the description says an automated system or software application presents the user with a list of needed resources or several selectable alternatives before the user acts on them: Model each such automated presentation of information or options as its own bpmn:serviceTask, placed in the order the description states and before the human work that depends on it. Do not omit these steps or merge them into the following bpmn:userTask.
rules.situation: the description says an automated system or software application presents the user with a list of needed resources or several selectable alternatives before the user acts on them

rules.instruction: When the description states that a set of candidate alternatives is first produced or requested as one action, and that choosing among those alternatives is described as a separate action: Model the production or request of the candidate alternatives as one task, and model the choice among them as a second task placed after it and connected by a sequence flow. Put each task in the lane of the actor the description names for that action. Label each task with the verb and main object the description uses. Do not merge generation and choice into one task, and do not add pools, message flows or events for parties the description does not state.
rules.situation: the description states that a set of candidate alternatives is first produced or requested as one action, and that choosing among those alternatives is described as a separate action
rules.source: learned guideline (refines FID-02), generalized from EXS-034

rules.instruction: When the description says that, for each required item, the user either already has it, gets it from others, or acquires it, so that only one of these alternatives applies to that item, and that the user then checks whether all required items are available: Model each per-item choice as an exclusive gateway with one outgoing branch per stated alternative, and do not use an inclusive gateway for it. Model a stated completeness check as its own exclusive gateway, placed after the item-level branches it depends on, with one branch for the complete case and one for the incomplete case. Keep the gateway's branches to the stated outcomes only.
rules.situation: the description says that, for each required item, the user either already has it, gets it from others, or acquires it, so that only one of these alternatives applies to that item, and that the user then checks whether all required items are available

rules.instruction: When The description states that an activity is carried out with or obtained from a specific party or source (for example, a task that gets items from a named group of people, or contacts a named party), so the source is part of the stated action.: Label the task with the verb the description uses for the action and name the party or source it involves, so the label keeps the stated source and does not generalize to a broader or different action such as receiving or handling items without saying where they come from.
rules.situation: The description states that an activity is carried out with or obtained from a specific party or source (for example, a task that gets items from a named group of people, or contacts a named party), so the source is part of the stated action.

rules.instruction: When the description states that the process begins with an action performed by a participant, not with a received message: Model a plain start event whose name does not repeat the described action or its result. Place a task for that action directly after the start event and before the activities that follow it. Do not let the start event itself stand for the action.
rules.situation: the description opens with a participant's action as its first step, and no separate triggering occurrence is named in the text

rules.instruction: When the description states an activity with a verb and object, and a candidate task label would add a purpose clause, a list of several items or options, or a restatement of a condition that the description attaches to other steps: Label the task with the verb and main object the description uses for that step, and keep the label to those words. Move purpose, item lists, options and conditions into the activity documentation or a linked data object, and do not add them to the task name.
rules.situation: the description states an activity with a verb and object, and a candidate task label would add a purpose clause, a list of several items or options, or a restatement of a condition that the description attaches to other steps
